demand.text: Time to shoot: a quick climb gives more freedom to shoot more balls, since less time climbing is more time scoring.

auto.text: In the Irving playoffs the top alliance ran 3310's high-scoring auto on the feeder side, which left 148 the hangar side.
In Roebling match 74 it hid cargo behind the hub in auto and in teleop.

cycle.text: Take cargo in, stop the indexer when a sensor sees a ball while the intake keeps running, then feed the two balls up an S-curve into a shooter that spins all match. Speed and hood angle come from a map of field positions.

endgame.text: Raise the "swords" and the elevator, pull up until the bumpers are about below the mid bar, react off the high bar along a cam, latch on the traversal bar, release and swing.
In one match a poster counts about six seconds from entering the hangar to the traversal.

gave_up.text: A team post says it built a top-heavy robot that had tipped over.

changed.text: At Waco the intake snapped almost half a dozen times; it got a second plate. At Irving a mesh tongue that gripped balls came with penalties; grippier bumpers and a motor that brings the intake in followed.
A top shooter wheel was added against backspin.
A recap video reports climber issues in the Roebling finals.

outcome.text: 65-7-0 in official play; finalist in the Roebling division; ranked 34 by championship OPR (52.35, Roebling).

solves.text: Grip cargo without snapping or collecting penalties

cost.text: With a single plate it snapped almost half a dozen times at Waco
Jams mostly happen at a place shown on camera, and not as much in the indexing

facts.text: Scaled up from the 2020 intake, with some changes to the geometry
Two plates of Lexan, about a quarter inch as captioned, where there was one; it had not snapped since, as of the Texas championship
Flex wheels on the bottom row grip better
A motor brings the entire intake in; it fitted once some VRMs were removed and sensors moved
The bumpers are covered in a slightly adhesive material that grips the balls

functions.name: Indexer and S-curve

solves.text: Always hold two balls and index them easily over a minimal distance

functions.type: indexer with an S-curve ball path

facts.text: An IR sensor stops the indexer when a ball is there; the intake is a separate subsystem and can still run
The S-curve runs straight into the shooter and holds two balls
Carried over from the Infinite Recharge game

functions.name: Shooter and hood

solves.text: Shoot with less backspin, from any point on the field

cost.text: The first prototype, with one wheel, put balls in that spun out again once a real goal was used

functions.type: flywheel with top wheel and variable hood

facts.text: A lower wheel from the previous year's prototype, and a top wheel added through a gear ratio to reduce backspin
The variable hood is the previous year's, scaled up
An interpolating tree map gives shooter speed and hood angle at any point on the field
Compression was chosen by testing wheel sizes for the lowest speed that works; as captioned, about
The motor sits low, because there is not enough space at the top

functions.name: Climber

solves.text: Reach the traversal bar quickly, to leave time for shooting

cost.text: A recap video reports climber issues in the Roebling finals

functions.type: elevator with arms that react off the high bar

facts.text: Of its three parts, only the elevator is controlled through the climb
The "swords" are powered up before the climb and then stay up; a third part deploys on a constant force spring
The robot reacts off the high bar along a cam surface, and past a bump the hooks pop into place on the traversal bar
Climb time at the Texas championship, as the team gives it, about
At the Texas championship it entered the hangar at 12 s left and latched at 3
In a Roebling match it scored 5 balls between 23 and 7 s left, entered the hangar at 6, touched the mid bar at 4 and was on the traversal at the buzzer
A poster says the cam geometry let it make a triple traversal with practically any two traversal-capable robots
A triple traversal with 5431 and 2687 in match 40 at Houston, the Texas championship, made a score of 160
A poster groups it with 125 as climbers that skip the high bar and lever off it to swing hooks up to traversal
A pit scouting list gives a swerve drive and no turret
A poster from memory lists it among the robots without pneumatics; a team that built a copy also names no use of pneumatics as something it learned

decisions.because: it gives more freedom to shoot more balls
it always holds two balls and indexes them easily over a minimal distance
decisions.instead_of: holding balls in an intake, which has not enough room

decisions.choice: Keep the shooter running all match
decisions.because: the speed stays consistent and no inertia has to be overcome each time
it finds the setting that gets there at the lowest speed, so no power is wasted
decisions.instead_of: a value that posts on the forum were giving

decisions.choice: Add a motor that brings the intake in
decisions.cost: some VRMs were removed and sensors moved to make room
